## Publish to PyPI with Trusted Publishing instead of a long-lived token

_medium · python_

**Rule.** Publish from CI through PyPI Trusted Publishing (OIDC). Do not store a PyPI API token in repository secrets.

**Why.** A long-lived token that leaks from a log or a compromised workflow lets anyone upload a release under your name until someone notices; an OIDC credential is valid for only 15 minutes and comes from the publisher configuration you registered on PyPI.

**Incorrect:**

```yaml
publish:
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  steps:
    - run: twine upload dist/*
      env:
        TWINE_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.PYPI_TOKEN }}
```

**Correct:**

```yaml
publish:
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  permissions:
    id-token: write
  steps:
    - uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
```

## Use Ruff as the only formatter and linter

_medium · python, ruff_

**Rule.** Format with `ruff format` and lint with `ruff check`, configured in `pyproject.toml`; do not add Black, Flake8 or isort next to it. Run both as pre-commit hooks.

**Why.** Two tools that format the same code disagree on edge cases and rewrite each other's output, so diffs fill with churn; one tool with one configuration removes the argument.

**Incorrect:**

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/psf/black
    hooks: [{id: black}]
  - repo: https://github.com/PyCQA/flake8
    hooks: [{id: flake8}]
  - repo: https://github.com/PyCQA/isort
    hooks: [{id: isort}]
```

**Correct:**

```yaml
repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff-pre-commit
    hooks:
      - id: ruff-check
        args: [--fix]
      - id: ruff-format
```

## Add a CI workflow that installs from the lockfile and runs the check suite

_medium · python, uv_

**Rule.** A new project on GitHub ships `.github/workflows/ci.yml` that runs on `push` and `pull_request`, installs uv with `astral-sh/setup-uv` at a pinned uv version, runs `uv sync --locked`, then runs the project's single check command (`make check`, see the Makefile note).

**Why.** Checks that only run on the author's machine are skipped under deadline, so a broken main branch is the first sign that a rule was never enforced.

**Incorrect:**

```yaml
on: push
jobs:
  test:
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: pip install -r requirements.txt && pytest
```

**Correct:**

```yaml
name: CI
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v9
        with:
          version: "0.13.6"
      - run: uv sync --locked
      - run: make check
```

**Exceptions.** A project without a Makefile lists the check commands directly after `uv sync --locked`. A project that is not on GitHub keeps the same steps in its own CI system.

## Use the src/ layout for libraries and CLI tools

_medium · python_

**Rule.** Put a library or CLI package under `src/<package_name>/`, not at the repository root.

**Why.** In a flat layout the working directory comes first on the import path, so tests pass against uninstalled sources and a file missing from the built package is only discovered after release.

**Incorrect:**

```text
mypkg/
  __init__.py
tests/
```

**Correct:**

```text
src/
  mypkg/
    __init__.py
tests/
```

**Exceptions.** Single scripts use PEP 723 inline metadata and `uv run script.py` instead of a package.

## Keep developer tools in [dependency-groups], not in optional-dependencies extras

_medium · python, uv_

**Rule.** Declare test, lint and docs tools under `[dependency-groups]` (PEP 735) and add them with `uv add --dev` or `--group`. Use `[project.optional-dependencies]` only for features users can opt into.

**Why.** Extras travel with the published package, so `pip install pkg[dev]` becomes a promise you must keep, while groups stay in the repository.

**Incorrect:**

```toml
[project.optional-dependencies]
dev = ["pytest", "ruff"]
```

**Correct:**

```toml
[dependency-groups]
dev = ["pytest", "ruff"]
```

## Define the check commands once in a Makefile that wraps uv run

_low · python, uv_

**Rule.** Put the check commands in one `check` target of a `Makefile` whose recipes only call `uv run ...`: the format check, the linter, the type checker and the tests. The README and CI call `make check`; CI installs with `uv sync --locked` before it.

**Why.** When the README, CI and the developer each spell out the commands, they drift apart, and CI passes a check nobody runs locally or the reverse.

**Incorrect:**

```make
test:
	pytest
```

**Correct:**

```make
.PHONY: install check

install:
	uv sync

check:
	uv run ruff format --check
	uv run ruff check
	uv run mypy
	uv run pytest
```

**Exceptions.** A project that already uses another task runner (`just`, `nox`, `poethepoet`) keeps it; the commands still live in one place and CI calls that runner.

## Enable Ruff rules that enforce logging conventions: G, LOG, T20, TRY400, TRY401

_low · python, ruff_

**Rule.** Add `G`, `LOG`, `T20`, `TRY400` and `TRY401` to the selected Ruff rules.

**Why.** Without `G` and `LOG` an f-string in `logger.info` or a root-logger call passes review, and without `T20` a stray `print()` reaches production.

**Incorrect:**

```toml
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B", "S"]
```

**Correct:**

```toml
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B", "S", "G", "LOG", "T20", "TRY400", "TRY401"]
```

**Exceptions.** Command-line entry points whose purpose is to print their result ignore `T201` in `per-file-ignores`.

## Enable Ruff PT rules to keep pytest tests in one style

_low · python, ruff, pytest_

**Rule.** Add `PT` to the selected Ruff families so tests follow pytest's own style.

**Why.** Without `PT` nothing flags a too-broad `pytest.raises` (PT011), a block with several statements (PT012) or a compound assert (PT018); the family also enforces pytest's fixture and parametrize conventions.

**Incorrect:**

```toml
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B", "S"]
```

**Correct:**

```toml
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B", "S", "PT"]
```

## Enforce docstrings with Ruff D rules set to the Google convention

_low · python, ruff_

**Rule.** Add `D` to the selected Ruff rule families, set `[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle] convention = "google"`, and ignore `D` under `tests/`.

**Why.** Without a convention the `D` families include NumPy-style section rules (D406-D409) that reject Google sections, plus mutually exclusive pairs; the convention selects one consistent set. It does not enforce the imperative mood (D401), so reviewers check that.

**Incorrect:**

```toml
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B", "S", "D"]
```

**Correct:**

```toml
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B", "S", "D"]

[tool.ruff.lint.pydocstyle]
convention = "google"

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**" = ["S101", "D"]
```

## Set Ruff's line length to 100 once, in pyproject.toml

_low · python, ruff_

**Rule.** Set `line-length = 100` once in `[tool.ruff]`. The formatter wraps to it and the `E501` lint rule flags what it cannot wrap. Do not wrap lines by hand to reach it.

**Why.** PEP 8 stops at 99 for teams that agree, so 100 is a deliberate team choice; without one value in the configuration the limit drifts per editor and reviews argue about wrapping instead of logic.

**Incorrect:**

```toml
[tool.ruff]
# line-length not set: the editor, CI and the docs each assume a different value
```

**Correct:**

```toml
[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100
```

## Enable Ruff rule families gradually, starting from E, F, I, UP, B and S

_low · python, ruff_

**Rule.** Select `E`, `F`, `I`, `UP`, `B` and `S` in `[tool.ruff.lint]`, which also sorts imports (`I`). Add `PTH`, `TC`, `FURB` and `TD` one family at a time, fixing the findings in the same change that enables each.

**Why.** Turning on every family at once produces thousands of findings nobody reviews; this starter set is the team's judgement of what catches real bugs first, and `S` ports Bandit's security checks from day one.

**Incorrect:**

```toml
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["ALL"]
```

**Correct:**

```toml
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = ["E", "F", "I", "UP", "B", "S"]

[tool.ruff.lint.per-file-ignores]
"tests/**" = ["S101"]
```

**Exceptions.** `S` flags every `assert` (S101), so ignore that rule under `tests/`, as shown.
